chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
'A town would not be hit by a Punishment while there are seven from the Momineen therein.'

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: The Momineen (believers) — those possessing true iman (faith), whose residence in a town constitutes a shield against divine chastisement
key_terms.سَبْعَةٌ: Seven — the minimum threshold of believers whose presence averts collective punishment from a community
key_terms.عَذَابٌ: Divine punishment or chastisement — the affliction sent by Allah upon a people as a consequence of their deeds
key_terms.قَرْيَةً: A town or settlement — any inhabited locality potentially subject to collective divine judgment
key_terms.يُصِيبُ: To strike or befall — used here for divinely ordained affliction reaching a community

ai.seo_question: Does the presence of believers protect a town from divine punishment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through a chain reaching Imam Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام), declares that divine punishment will not descend upon any town so long as seven true believers reside within it. The narration affirms the immense spiritual worth of the mu'min and their function as a divinely ordained protection for the broader community. It is a foundational statement in Shia theology regarding the mercy Allah extends to settlements on account of the faithful dwelling therein.
